title: Does One Jailbreak Transfer Predict Homogeneity Elsewhere? Linking Attack Transfer to Output Convergence

original_idea.body:
# Does One Jailbreak Transfer Predict Homogeneity Elsewhere? Linking Attack Transfer to Output Convergence

**Problem:** Jailbreak transferability is attributed to shared representations, and Hivemind shows shared outputs - but no one has tested whether the models MOST similar in benign output homogeneity are also the most jailbreak-cross-transferable.

**Direction:** Measure pairwise benign output homogeneity and pairwise jailbreak transfer success using public jailbreak prompts. Test whether a homogeneity score predicts transferability.

**Why it matters:** If benign homogeneity predicts shared vulnerability, defenders get an early-warning metric computable without any attack data.

**Relevant context:** Jailbreak Transferability from Shared Representations (arXiv:2506.12913); Artificial Hivemind.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a cheap benign-similarity early-warning proxy for shared attack surface is a defensible defensive deliverable on a recognized robustness pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two measurements (benign homogeneity + public jailbreak transfer) plus a correlation; uses existing jailbreaks, no novel attacks.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused correlation test with two clear measurements; modest dual-workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public prompts/models, no internal access; third-party early-warning metric.

novelty.reasoning: Jointly correlating benign homogeneity with transferability appears largely unmeasured.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The explicit benign-homogeneity-as-vulnerability-proxy correlation seems unstudied.
